content:
Alex Martinez: Kicking off a thread to lock template catalog v1. We keep circling RAG vs agents vs “combo”. Need a decision this week so docs + repo scaffolding can start.

Talia Benson: +1. Can we also decide default backends (vector DB / queue / storage) so we don’t boil the ocean?

Wei Chen: For docs IA it’s much easier if we have 2-3 clear “choose your path” entries.

Dana Lo: Proposal: v1 ships exactly 3 templates:
1) RAG service (query API) + ingestion worker
2) Agents (tool calling patterns)
3) RAG+Agent (retrieval tool + planner/executor)
No more.

Monica Patel: Works. But we need to be careful re “agents” expectations. Should be simple orchestrator, not framework.

Renee Sullivan: From advocacy POV: 3 templates is perfect. I can do demos around each. Also gives us a story: start w/ RAG, then tools, then combine.

Alex Martinez: Cool. Next: backends. We said “1-2 common backends” in scope. What’s default for vector store?

Dana Lo: Please not 4 different options. For TypeScript especially, adapters explode fast.

Mateusz Zielinski: If we want Private-friendly defaults, avoid SaaS-only assumptions. Something people can run in Docker / k8s.

Wei Chen: Agree. Also: whatever we pick needs to be explainable in 2 paragraphs and runnable in <15m.

Logan Wright: From telemetry angle, backend choice matters less than consistent request IDs + spans. But if we pick a backend that requires a bunch of extra services, onboarding will suffer.

Naomi Feldman: Security lens: avoid patterns that push folks to embed credentials in code. If we pick a SaaS vector DB as default, make sure we’re not normalizing long-lived API keys in `.env` with no guidance.

Monica Patel: Candidates:
- Postgres + pgvector (local + prod-ish)
- Qdrant (easy Docker)
- Pinecone/Weaviate (popular managed)
- “Chroma” (super easy but feels toy)

Dana Lo: +1 for Postgres/pgvector as default. Everyone already knows Postgres. Also easy path to Dedicated/Private.

Renee Sullivan: But will devs bounce if they have to run Postgres locally?

Dana Lo: Docker Compose can do it. One command.

Wei Chen: If the quickstart is `docker compose up` + `uv run` / `pnpm dev`, that’s fine.

Talia Benson: What about a managed option too? A bunch of customers will already have Pinecone.

Monica Patel: We can do an adapter interface. Default impl = pgvector. Optional adapter = Pinecone (or Qdrant cloud) behind a feature flag.

Mateusz Zielinski: Careful: “optional adapters” quickly become “we support it” in users’ heads. If we do 2, we need a support matrix.

Alex Martinez: Ok, rule: v1 supports one default backend (first-class, tested). Second backend only if it’s low maintenance.

Dana Lo: pgvector is the one. For second, I’d pick Pinecone because demand. But can we push it to v1.1?

Renee Sullivan: I’m fine demoing pgvector. It’s also a good “production minded” message.

Wei Chen: Docs can say “Default: Postgres (pgvector). Extension point: `VectorStore` interface. If you’re using Pinecone/Weaviate/etc, swap adapter.”

Logan Wright: +1. Also fewer moving parts = fewer telemetry gaps and fewer “why is my trace broken” tickets.

Naomi Feldman: If pgvector is default, we should include:
- least-privilege DB user in compose
- note on TLS + creds in prod
- don’t log raw docs / embeddings

Monica Patel: For ingestion pipeline, do we also need a queue? Or can we keep it simple with a background worker + polling?

Dana Lo: Keep it simple in v1: ingestion worker is just a separate process reading from a local “jobs” table or a directory. Queues add another system.

Renee Sullivan: For the reference app later we can add Redis / SQS / whatever.

Talia Benson: If we do “directory watcher” ingestion, we need to be explicit about production upgrade path.

Wei Chen: + we need to avoid teaching unsafe file upload patterns.

Monica Patel: Suggestion: ingestion is triggered by an explicit API endpoint (authenticated) that accepts a file path reference (not raw file upload) in local mode, and a “TODO: hook to your blob store” note for prod.

Naomi Feldman: Please no “upload arbitrary file into server” examples by default.

Alex Martinez: Agree. Keep ingestion local-only workflow safe and obvious.

Mateusz Zielinski: Back to vector store: pgvector in Docker Compose is very k8s/Private aligned. For Dedicated/Private docs later we can recommend managed Postgres or customer’s existing Postgres.

Logan Wright: Telemetry: whichever backend, make sure we add spans around “embed”, “vector_search”, “rerank” (if any), and tag with `vector_store.type=pgvector` so dashboards can slice.

Dana Lo: Ok. Can we lock decisions?

Alex Martinez: Draft decision:
- Template catalog v1 = RAG, Agents, RAG+Agents
- Default vector backend = Postgres + pgvector
- Adapter interface exists; non-default backends are “community / optional” until we commit support
- Ingestion = separate worker process, no queue dependency in v1
Any objections?

Renee Sullivan: :thumbsup:

Wei Chen: :thumbsup: (and I’ll update docs outline to match)

Monica Patel: :thumbsup: but note: for Agents template, we should keep tool calling examples limited + safe (allow-list, timeouts). Not part of this thread, but please.

Naomi Feldman: :thumbsup: with security notes in README + `.env.example` should be minimal and contain comments.

Logan Wright: :thumbsup: I’ll add to my list: span/attr naming guidance for vector store + ingestion.

Talia Benson: Great. Action items?

Alex Martinez: Action items:
- @Dana Lo write 1-pager in Confluence: catalog v1 + backend decision + what’s explicitly NOT supported
- @Wei Chen align docs IA (“Choose your template”)
- @Monica Patel sanity check SDK surface needed for all 3 templates
- @Naomi Feldman drop security notes we must include (secrets + PII)
We’ll revisit “second backend” after dogfood.

Dana Lo: Ack. I’ll post a draft EOD.

Wei Chen: Thanks all. This unblocks a bunch.

Renee Sullivan: Once we have pgvector decided, I’ll start prepping a simple “support agent RAG” demo flow using that stack.

Alex Martinez: Perfect. Closing the loop here once the doc is up.
